recognize_zh: 超活體染色（supravital stain）下幾乎每個紅血球內都有深藍色沉澱的顆粒或網狀物質，箭頭所指細胞內含粗大團聚的包涵體；大量紅血球含沉澱物提示不穩定血紅素造成的 Heinz 小體與網狀紅血球增多，但本圖解析度下難以完全區分兩者。
features: Supravital-stained smear with nearly all red cells containing dark blue precipitated inclusions
Inclusions vary from fine reticular/filamentous material to coarse clumped granules (arrow)
Some inclusions are coarse and irregular rather than the evenly distributed fine 'golf ball' pattern of HbH
Background shows stained platelets and plasma debris; resolution limits separating reticulocyte reticulum from Heinz bodies
describe_en: Supravitally stained peripheral blood smear shows that the large majority of red cells contain dark blue precipitated material, ranging from fine reticular networks to coarse clumped granular inclusions (arrow). The pattern indicates marked reticulocytosis with intraerythrocytic precipitates rather than the uniform golf-ball stippling of hemoglobin H. At this magnification reticulocyte RNA cannot be reliably distinguished from membrane-bound Heinz bodies, which should be confirmed with crystal violet staining, heat/isopropanol stability testing and globin gene sequencing. Findings are suggestive of hereditary hemolytic anemia due to an unstable hemoglobin.

ddx.vs: HbH inclusions are numerous, fine and evenly distributed ('golf ball') after incubation with brilliant cresyl blue, rather than coarse eccentric clumps.
Heinz bodies occur episodically after oxidant exposure with bite/blister cells and a low G6PD activity, while unstable hemoglobin gives chronic hemolysis and positive heat stability test.
Reticulocytes show fine reticular RNA networks only and the smear shows spherocytes with positive EMA binding, without Heinz body precipitates.
Features coarse basophilic stippling on Wright stain rather than supravital Heinz bodies, confirmed by enzyme assay.
